## Purpose and Topology
CK-X is a Docker-composed Kubernetes certification simulator for CKA, CKAD, CKS, and other lab tracks. It combines a browser exam UI, a Node.js facilitator API, isolated jump-host/cluster environments, and browser-accessible terminal/desktop sessions. Primary deployment is `docker-compose.yaml`; installation delegates to `scripts/install.sh` or `scripts/install.ps1`.

## Browser Exam Client
The static web client supplies landing, exam, results, answer, and feedback pages. Exam orchestration includes question retrieval, countdown/wake-lock behavior, answer/result interactions, plus terminal and remote-desktop clients. Key paths: `app/public/exam.html`, `app/public/js/exam.js`, `app/public/js/components/exam-api.js`, `app/public/js/components/terminal-service.js`, `app/public/js/components/remote-desktop-service.js`.

## App Edge Server
`app/server.js` is the web-facing Node.js entry point. Its routing/static services expose the public client and proxy or broker user-facing terminal and VNC/remote-desktop access. This is the boundary between browser code and runtime session services. Key paths: `app/server.js`, `app/services/route-service.js`, `app/services/ssh-terminal.js`, `app/services/vnc-service.js`.

## Facilitator API and Session Orchestration
A separate Node.js facilitator service owns exam metadata, assessment execution, SSH access, and remote-desktop lifecycle endpoints. Controllers/routes form the API boundary; services coordinate examination state with jump hosts and metrics. Redis is an explicit state/infrastructure dependency via its client utility. Key paths: `facilitator/src/app.js`, `facilitator/src/controllers/examController.js`, `facilitator/src/controllers/assessmentController.js`, `facilitator/src/services/examService.js`, `facilitator/src/services/jumphostService.js`, `facilitator/src/utils/redisClient.js`.

## Lab Content and Evaluation Contract
Labs are content-driven under a shared catalog, organized by certification and numbered exam. Each exam couples configuration and assessment metadata with setup scripts that establish a task environment and validation scripts that inspect the learner’s resulting Docker/Kubernetes state. Answers are separately stored for reveal/review. Representative paths: `facilitator/assets/exams/labs.json`, `facilitator/assets/exams/cka/001/config.json`, `facilitator/assets/exams/cka/001/assessment.json`, `facilitator/assets/exams/cka/001/scripts/setup`, `facilitator/assets/exams/cka/001/scripts/validation`.

## Isolated Practical Environment
The jump host prepares and cleans per-exam environments, acting as the execution location for learner commands and evaluator interactions. A containerized Kubernetes runtime uses k3d tooling and lifecycle scripts; this provides the real cluster surface validated by lab scripts. Key paths: `jumphost/scripts/prepare-exam-env.sh`, `jumphost/scripts/cleanup-exam-env.sh`, `kind-cluster/entrypoint.sh`, `kind-cluster/scripts/env-setup`, `kind-cluster/scripts/env-cleanup`.

## Remote Access and Deployment Runtime
Docker containers package each plane: web app, facilitator, jump host, cluster, remote terminal, remote desktop, and Nginx front end. Remote desktop has a Python agent and startup path, while Nginx is the HTTP reverse-proxy/static edge. Material external/runtime technologies are Docker/Docker-in-Docker, k3d/Kubernetes, Node.js, Redis, Nginx, SSH, VNC, and ConSol headless VNC. Key paths: `app/Dockerfile`, `facilitator/Dockerfile`, `remote-desktop/agent.py`, `remote-desktop/startup.sh`, `nginx/default.conf`.
